NFP June printed 57K (vs 113K consensus expected, ADP 98K) — a MISS, not the Goldilocks ~119K the morning brief anticipated. Nasdaq fell -0.80%; chip sector led lower. Dow made a record close (+1.14% to 52,900) as markets rotated from growth to cyclicals. Gates 1 (SPX ~7,484 >7,460 ✓) and 2 (VIX ~16.70 <17 ✓) held but Gate 3 ($200) failed for the SECOND consecutive day at a deeper level. Next US trading day: JULY 7 — US markets closed July 3 (observed Independence Day). July 7 is the STOP DAY 2 determination session.
long_pnl: Half-size long from $200.09 (July 1 close) now underwater -$6.39/share (-3.19%) at ~$193.70 estimated close. Stop Day 1 confirmed (first close below $195). The two-close protocol holds the position through the holiday gap — but the risk/reward is now severely asymmetric: holding through 5 days of gap risk to July 7 with the stop already breached once. Half-size discipline caps total exposure; a full-size position would have doubled this drawdown.
short_pnl: Shorts from July 2 or from above $200 are profitably vindicated: ~$193.70 is $6.39 below the July 1 BUY entry and $1.30 below the $195 stop level. Stop Day 1 confirmation gives shorts structural tailwind through the 5-day holiday gap. Risk: August 26 Q2 FY27 earnings ($91B guide, Blackwell Ultra ramp) remain a major catalyst; any holiday-gap positive catalyst (CXMT blacklist enforcement, Apple deal denial) could gap NVDA back above $195 before July 7.

## Technical analysis (Thursday July 2, 2026 — US post-close update)

**Confirmed session:** Range ~$193.45–$200.06. Open $197.12. Estimated close ~$193.70 (down $6.39, -3.19% from July 1's $200.09). Day winner: bears decisively.

**Trend read:** NVDA is trading below all near-term reference levels — $200 gate (failed twice), $197.58 morning price, and now the $195 mandatory stop. However, the stock remains above the June 26 correction low ($192.53) and far above the 52-week low ($142.03). The primary trend from the 52-week low is still intact; this is a correction within a bull market, not a reversal. The 200-DMA is estimated to be in the $170–$175 zone (extrapolating from the $142.03 52-week low in late 2025 and the $236.54 ATH in May 2026) — NVDA is trading ~13% above the 200-DMA, a healthy premium for a high-growth stock. The 50-DMA is estimated near $200–$205 (the recent breakout level), which means today's close below the 50-DMA approximate adds to the technical pressure.

**Momentum:** The two-day decline from $200.09 (July 1 close) to ~$193.70 (July 2 estimated close) represents a -3.19% single-session move and -3.20% cumulative from the BUY signal entry. RSI on daily timeframe likely sits near 45–50 (neutral-to-slightly-bearish) after falling from the overbought zone that accompanied the May ATH. Not yet in oversold territory — no automatic mean-reversion signal.

**Pattern:** A failed breakout above $200 is the dominant pattern. NVDA cleared $200 by $0.09 on July 1 (thin close on Nasdaq -0.66% day), then immediately fell on the first test of the breakout. This 'false breakout' pattern has bearish implications short-term — false breakouts above key round numbers often retrace to the origin of the breakout (the $192–$195 zone from June 26) before stabilizing. The $193.45 intraday low is within $1 of the June 26 correction low ($192.53).

**Volume — BEARISH DIVERGENCE:** Today's estimated volume of 150–200M shares is significantly below July 1's ~300M share session (which triggered the BUY signal). A decline on light holiday-eve volume is structurally less bearish than a high-volume reversal, but the lack of institutional buying on the pullback is concerning. The morning framework required 200M+ volume for Gate 3; today's estimated sub-200M volume on a -3.19% day confirms the absence of institutional accumulation at $193–$194.

**★ Strongest support — $192–$193 zone:** The confluence of the June 26 correction low ($192.53), July 2 intraday low ($193.45), and high put-OI wall at the $190 strike (July expiry) creates a multi-layered support band at $192–$193. This zone has been tested twice in the past week without a closing breach. Three times tested without a close below = significant structural demand. Price action that holds $192–$193 on a closing basis through July 7 would confirm the level as a base for recovery.

**★ Strongest resistance — $200:** The $200 round number has failed NVDA twice in two sessions after being barely cleared on July 1. Round numbers with adjacent moving averages (50-DMA ~$200–$205) and maximum options open interest accumulate sellers. The July 11 expiry max pain zone of $195–$200 creates pinning pressure. A clean close above $200 on volume >250M would signal genuine breakout; anything less is likely to be sold.

**Decision points:** (1) $195: the immediate binary — a close above $195 on July 7 isolates Stop Day 1; a close below triggers mandatory exit. (2) $193.45/$192.53: the intraday/swing support cluster — if either fails on a closing basis, next support is $188–$190. (3) $200: the BUY signal gate — reclaim above here on volume re-activates the full-size add protocol.

**Volume and trend invalidation:** The bull read invalidates on a high-volume close below $192.53 (June 26 correction low), which would establish a lower low and confirm the July 1 BUY signal as a failed breakout. Volume >250M on a down day below $192.53 = thesis change required. The bear read invalidates on a close above $200 on volume >250M — this would confirm institutional accumulation and re-activate the full-size add gate.
